Layer 2 — Custom Source Interface (Your Implementation)
🔌 BaseSource → CustomSource
mlrun.datastore.sources.BaseSource
to_dataframe()
Reads data from your source and returns a Pandas or Spark DataFrame
is_online
Boolean flag — True for real-time streaming, False for batch ingestion
get_spark_df()
Optional — returns a Spark DataFrame for large-scale distributed processing
kind (str)
Unique identifier string registered in MLRun's source registry
Override to_dataframe() Register kind= Schema Validation Auth Handling Error Handling

📦
FeatureSet
mlrun.feature_store.FeatureSet
Defines schema, entities, and features
Calls FeatureSet.ingest(source)
Triggers your CustomSource automatically
Stores lineage and metadata
ingest() deploy_ingestion_service()

Feature Registry
Catalog & Versioning

Layer 4 — Custom Target Interface (Your Implementation)
🎯 BaseTarget → CustomTarget
mlrun.datastore.targets.BaseStoreTarget
write_dataframe()
Writes the transformed DataFrame to your target store
get_table_artifact()
Returns a reference artifact MLRun uses to track this target
as_df()
Reads back data from target — used during offline serving
kind (str)
Unique identifier string registered in MLRun's target registry
Override write_dataframe() Register kind= Partitioning Upsert Logic Connection Pooling

Layer 6 — FeatureVector (Serving Interface)
🧩 FeatureVector — Cross-FeatureSet Feature Assembly
mlrun.feature_store.FeatureVector
get_offline_features()
Joins features from multiple FeatureSets for batch training datasets
get_online_feature_service()
Returns a live service that retrieves features in real-time for inference
Entity Join Logic
Joins on entity keys (e.g. customer_id) across all referenced FeatureSets
Point-in-Time Joins
Ensures no data leakage — features retrieved as-of the label timestamp
Multi-FeatureSet Join Point-in-Time Correct No Data Leakage Online + Offline Consistency
